newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices resume upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices resume upward trend.

text.p: Australian wool prices strengthened this week at sales in Sydney and Adelaide, Australian Council of Wool Exporters said in its weekly wool report.
The eastern market indicator rose 15 cents to 675 cents per kilogram clean, while the western market indicator fell two cents to 629 kg clean over the week.
Wesfarmers Dalgety said that following the correction of last week, prices resumed their upward trend.
"Prices strengthened progressively for the rest of the week due to widespread buyer activity," Wesfarmers said.
The council said there was strong interest in the better and finer types in Sydney, and also in the traditional South Australian types which will be in the shorter supply for the rest of the season.
"Purchases for China were an important factor in the market, together with there being no sales rostered for next week," it said.
A total of 104,675 bales were offered at auction with a pass in rate of 11.12 percent.
Trade competition was led by Japanese and Chinese buyers with support from local mills and other secotrs of the trade.
In the futures market a total of 204 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract for the week ending May 15.
Open interest increased by 44 contracts to close at 962. The August 1976 contract closed 40 cents up at 817 cents a kg clean.
Sales will resume in two weeks at auctions in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with 114,300 bales rostered for sale.
